verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents an official MCP server that lets agents create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events and edit Functions, with OAuth for interactive clients and API keys for headless use. A Management HTTP API also covers workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions, and Live Events shows streaming delivery results. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven pipeline management, explicit MCP-side mention of creating sources (only destinations and streams are named), and a machine-readable OpenAPI spec reachable at the standard paths the probe checked.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can manage the pipeline itself — create sources and destinations, wire streams, inspect deliveries — through a documented API or MCP server

citations.quote: Jitsu runs an MCP server, so AI agents can manage your pipeline directly: create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events, and edit Functions.
Jitsu exposes an HTTP API for managing workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions.
A public Management API for every Jitsu instance, with a full OpenAPI 3.0 reference at docs.jitsu.com/api.
Everything you can see in Live Events — function logs, warehouse batch statuses, streaming delivery results, and dead-lettered events
Point your agent at `https://use.jitsu.com/mcp`, approve it once in the browser, and it can run your data pipeline for you.
